name: Northwind Studio
about: A small fictional design and software studio in Sofia: a bank pilot being priced and signed, a designer being hired, a site relaunch that moved, team notes, a private health note, a newsletter, a Bulgarian email, and one of each thing a night of dreaming finds (an old and a new door code, a moved flight, an answered ask, a receipt stored twice, a rule that is a fact, a contradiction, a thread with mixed sensitivity). 37 items and 11 evaluation questions.

items.title: Lumen Bank pilot
items.text: Run a three-month pilot of our onboarding app for Lumen Bank's branch staff. Owner: Alex. Operations: Elena. Development: Ivan.

items.title: Hire a second designer
items.text: Hire a second product designer to work beside Sofia. Elena runs the search.

items.title: Northwind site relaunch
items.text: Relaunch northwind.example with the new case studies. Ivan builds, and Sofia designs.

items.title: Pilot pricing
items.text:
Hello Alex,

I am getting in touch to request a quote for a 3-month pilot for 40 branch staff. Please include the pricing for the pilot and make clear what is covered by the quoted amount. Our budget ceiling for this work is 18,000 EUR, so it would be helpful to understand whether the proposed price can fit within that limit.

Could you also confirm whether training is included in the pilot? If it is, please outline what training is covered in the quote. If training is not included, please indicate that clearly and show any related cost separately, so we can assess the overall amount against our budget ceiling.

Please send the quote within a week. It would be useful if it identifies the duration, the number of staff covered, the total price, and any items that are not included. If any part of the pricing depends on details that are not set out here, please note what information you would need from us to prepare the quote.

We are looking for pricing for the 3-month pilot described above, rather than a longer-term proposal at this stage. Please let me know if you can provide the quote within that timeframe, and whether the training question can be addressed in the same response.

Thank you for your help. I look forward to reviewing the quote.

Best,
Daniel

items.title: Re: Pilot pricing
items.text:
Hello Daniel,

Thank you for following up on the pilot pricing. For the three-month pilot, our quoted price is 16,500 EUR. Training is included in that amount, and the pilot will be delivered on site in Sofia.

The payment schedule is 50% upfront and the remaining 50% at the end of the pilot. This keeps the pricing and timing straightforward: half is due upfront, and half is due at the end. The quoted amount covers the three-month pilot with training included, as noted above.

For the sequence of work, the onboarding flow that I call Module A is the first deliverable. I wanted to make that ordering clear alongside the pricing, so you can see what comes first within the pilot. Module A is the starting deliverable, and the engagement is planned as a three-month pilot on site in Sofia.

To recap, the quote is 16,500 EUR for the three-month pilot, training is included, delivery is on site in Sofia, and payment is split 50% upfront and 50% at the end. Module A, the onboarding flow, is the first deliverable.

Please let me know if you would like me to clarify any part of the quoted price, payment split, location, or first deliverable. I am happy to keep the details aligned as you review the pilot pricing.

Best,
Alex

items.title: Re: Pilot pricing
items.text:
Hello Alex,

The price is fine from our side, and we are comfortable with the amount as proposed. There is one point we need to clarify before we can move forward: our procurement rule allows no more than 30% upfront. Could you confirm whether the payment schedule can be arranged within that limit? If the current schedule requires a larger upfront payment, please let me know what alternative would be possible while keeping the agreed price unchanged.

I also wanted to ask about the training arrangement. Would it be possible to deliver the training remotely rather than on site? A remote format would save travel, so it may be a practical option for us. Please let me know whether remote delivery is available and whether it would affect the price or the training arrangements in any way.

We have not yet decided how many staff would start in the first group. We are still considering either 20 or 40 staff, and I will confirm which option we choose once that decision has been made. For now, please treat the starting group size as undecided rather than assuming either number.

Once we have clarified the upfront payment limit and whether remote training is possible, we will be in a better position to review the remaining details on our side. Please share what options you can support, and we can take it from there.

Best,
Daniel

items.title: Re: Pilot pricing
items.text:
Hi Daniel,

Thank you for sending through the pilot pricing details. I am happy to confirm that I agree with the proposed payment structure: 30% upfront and the remaining 70% at the end. The price will stay at 16,500 EUR.

I also confirm that the training will be delivered remotely. This keeps the arrangements for the pilot clear, with the payment split and training format set out as agreed. I will prepare the contract draft and send it to you by Friday.

For clarity, the agreed figures are 30% upfront, 70% at the end, and a total price of 16,500 EUR. The training is remote, and the contract draft is the next item I will provide. I am confirming these points here so that the written draft can reflect the same terms. I will send that draft by Friday, as promised, for your review.

The draft will reflect the agreed price, payment schedule, and remote training arrangement. Please review those points when you receive it, and let me know if anything in the draft does not match what we have agreed. Until then, I will proceed on the basis described above. I appreciate your coordination on the pilot pricing, and I look forward to getting the draft to you by Friday.

Best,
Alex

items.title: Signed: Lumen pilot
items.text:
Hi Alex,

I'm pleased to confirm that the contract is signed. The pilot starts on 1 November with 40 staff.

Could you please send me the kickoff agenda by Thursday? Please include a 30-minute walkthrough of Module A. Having the agenda in advance will give me a chance to review the planned topics and understand how the kickoff is expected to flow. The walkthrough should be included as part of the agenda, with its 30-minute duration noted, so that this part of the session is clear to everyone reviewing the plan.

Could you also let me know who your day-to-day contact will be for the pilot? It would be useful to know who to reach out to with routine questions or when coordination is needed. Please share their name and, if appropriate, the best way to contact them. I'm asking so that we know where to direct communications once the pilot is under way.

For now, the two items I need are the kickoff agenda, including the Module A walkthrough, and confirmation of your day-to-day contact. Please send the agenda by Thursday, and let me know about the contact when you can. If there is anything you need from me to prepare the agenda, feel free to ask.

Thanks for helping us get the preparation in order. I look forward to reviewing the agenda and to getting started with the pilot on 1 November.

Best,
Daniel

items.title: Designer shortlist
items.text:
Hi Alex,

I am sending you the shortlist of three product designers for consideration: Ana Petkova, Boris Nedev, and Mila Toneva.

Among the three candidates, Ana has the strongest portfolio and brings fintech experience. Based on those points, I recommend that we interview Ana first. That would give us an opportunity to discuss her work and experience directly before deciding on next steps for the shortlist.

The salary expectations across the candidates range from 3,200 to 3,600 BGN a month. I am sharing that range alongside the names so it is included in our initial review. I have not ranked Boris or Mila against Ana, and the information available here does not support a further comparison between them.

My recommendation is therefore limited to the clearest differentiators noted for Ana: the strength of her portfolio, together with her fintech experience. We can use the interview to learn more about her background, while keeping Boris Nedev and Mila Toneva in the shortlist. This email is intended to make the shortlist and recommendation easy to review; it does not add conclusions beyond the details above.

Please let me know whether you agree with interviewing Ana first.

Best,
Elena

items.title: Re: Designer shortlist
items.text:
Hi Elena,

I've decided we should interview Ana and Mila for the designer shortlist. Please keep the budget at no more than 3,500 BGN a month. Let me know if you need anything else from me.

Best,
Alex

items.title: Ana's interview
items.text:
Hi Alex,

I wanted to share the outcome of Ana's interview. It went very well, and Sofia liked her. Ana asks for 3,800 BGN a month, which is above the 3,500 budget. No decision has been made about whether to adjust the budget or proceed with an offer at the current amount.

Could you decide by Monday which option you want us to take? We can raise the budget to meet Ana's request, or offer 3,500 with two remote days. Those are the two possibilities to consider at this point. The first would mean moving above the budget, while the second would keep the amount at 3,500 and include two remote days. Please let me know which direction you would like to take by Monday, so I can follow your decision in communicating the next step to Ana.

Until then, I will leave the terms unresolved and will not present either route as the final offer. The key decision is whether the budget can be raised from 3,500 to accommodate the 3,800 monthly request, or whether we should stay at 3,500 and include two remote days instead. Your decision is still open, and I am asking you to choose between these options by Monday.

Thanks,
Elena

items.title: Relaunch plan
items.text:
Hi Alex,

I am planning the site relaunch for 15 October. The relaunch will include new case studies, faster pages, and a contact form that writes to the CRM. To keep that plan on track, I need the final designs by 5 October.

Please treat 5 October as the date for the completed designs, rather than an earlier draft or an open set of design questions. Having the final version by then will give me a clear basis for planning the relaunch around the work that is ready. The three parts of the relaunch should remain visible in the plan: the new case studies, the faster pages, and the contact form with its CRM connection.

When you send the designs, please make clear that they are final. If anything is still unresolved, please identify it plainly so I can distinguish it from the final design set. I am not asking for additional scope here, only for designs that support the relaunch planned for 15 October.

Please let me know whether you can provide the final designs by 5 October. If you see a concern with that date, please flag it so we can understand the status of the plan without changing the relaunch date by assumption.

Thanks,
Ivan

items.title: Re: Relaunch plan
items.text:
Hi Ivan,

I wanted to follow up on the relaunch plan. The designs are not ready yet, because the case-study photos are late. With those photos still outstanding, I do not think we should treat the current designs as ready for the relaunch.

I propose that we move the relaunch to 29 October. That would give us a more realistic date for the plan, rather than proceeding while the designs are not ready. I would prefer that we make the change clearly now, so the relaunch date reflects the state of the work and is not based on an assumption that the photos will arrive in time.

Please let me know whether you agree with moving the relaunch to 29 October. If you see a reason to keep the current date, we can discuss it, but my recommendation is to reschedule. The main point is that the designs are not ready, and the late case-study photos are the reason. Moving the date would make the plan consistent with that status.

I am not suggesting a change to anything else in the relaunch plan. My proposal is only to move the relaunch to 29 October because the case-study photos are late and the designs are not ready. Once we have agreed on the date, we can use it as the relaunch date in the plan.

Best,
Sofia

items.title: Re: Relaunch plan
items.text:
Hi Ivan and Sofia,

I've decided that the relaunch moves to 29 October. Sofia, you own the hero images for the relaunch. This is the plan we will follow for the relaunch.

Best,
Alex

items.title: This week: 12 portfolio trends
items.text:
Hi Alex,

This week, we're looking at 12 ways to make a portfolio feel clearer, more personal, and easier to explore. Consider these as starting points, and choose the ideas that fit your work.

1. Lead with a concise introduction. [Explore the idea](https://example.com/intro)
2. Use a focused selection of projects. [See a layout](https://example.com/selection)
3. Give each project a clear title. [Review examples](https://example.com/titles)
4. Add a short note about your role. [Try this approach](https://example.com/role)
5. Show process alongside finished work. [Browse process layouts](https://example.com/process)
6. Use captions to add useful context. [Find caption ideas](https://example.com/captions)
7. Let images have room to breathe. [View spacing tips](https://example.com/spacing)
8. Keep navigation simple and visible. [Explore navigation](https://example.com/navigation)
9. Build a consistent visual rhythm. [See composition prompts](https://example.com/rhythm)
10. Make contact details easy to find. [Check a contact page](https://example.com/contact)
11. Review the experience on a small screen. [Use this checklist](https://example.com/mobile)
12. Refresh older work with new context. [Read the update guide](https://example.com/refresh)

A useful portfolio does not need to follow every trend. Start with one small change, then review whether it helps visitors understand what you do and how you think. You can also collect feedback from someone unfamiliar with your projects: notice where they pause, what they ask about, and which details help them move through the work.

For more inspiration, save a few examples you enjoy and note what makes them easy to navigate. A clear structure and thoughtful explanations can make a portfolio feel considered without adding unnecessary decoration.

See you next week,

Design

items.title: What we mean by Module A
items.text:
Hi Elena, Ivan, and Sofia,

I want to clarify what we mean by Module A. Module A is our name for the onboarding flow for Lumen's branch staff. It includes sign in, the five training lessons, and the quiz. Module B, reporting, comes after the pilot.

Best,
Alex

items.title: Module A estimate
items.text:
Hi Alex,

My current estimate for Module A is 12 developer days. Please treat that as the estimate based on the information available now, rather than as a confirmed total, because one dependency remains unclear.

Lumen's single sign-on is not documented. Without that documentation, I cannot tell whether the SSO work changes the effort for Module A. If it does, the additional effort could be a week. That is a caveat to the 12 developer day estimate, not a change to the estimate itself, and the extra week is possible rather than certain.

Could you get the SSO documentation from Daniel before the kickoff? Having it beforehand will let us review the information and assess whether the estimate needs to account for the SSO uncertainty. If the documentation does not change the picture, we can retain the 12 developer day estimate. If it does indicate additional work, we can discuss the possible week of extra effort with that information in hand.

For now, I would keep the 12 developer days as the working estimate and make the undocumented SSO dependency visible when we discuss Module A. Please let me know once you have the documentation, so that I can check its impact before kickoff. The main thing I want to avoid is treating the estimate as final while this point is still unresolved.

Thanks,
Ivan
